Claim 281 (Currently amended): A cutting blade comprising: a blade core having a support wall extending from a driving portion to a perimeter portion; at least one working element supported by the support wall at the perimeter portion; and a nozzle in the support wall between the driving portion and the perimeter portion, the nozzle including a wall defining an opening facing outward from the support wall, wherein the nozzle is supported in a nozzle body, the nozzle body being supported in the support wall of the blade core, and the nozzle wall is a first wall defining a first opening and wherein the nozzle includes a second wall defining a second opening facing outward in a second direction from the support wall.

Claim 282 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 281, wherein the nozzle is supported in a nozzle body, wherein the nozzle body is supported in the support wall of the blade core and wherein the nozzle wall is a first wall defining a first opening and wherein the nozzle includes a second wall defining a second opening facing outward in a second direction from the support wall.

Claim 283 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 282, wherein the first and second openings of the nozzle face in different directions.

Claim 284 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 281, further including a fluid flow element in the blade core extending from the driving portion to the nozzle.

Claim 290 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 281, wherein the nozzle is removable.

Claim 291 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 290, wherein the nozzle includes a wall defining an opening that opens in a direction toward the working element.

Claim 293 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 281, further including an inlet fitting having a channel into which an upstream tube end extends.

Claim 294 (Currently amended): The cutting blade of claim 293, wherein the inlet fitting includes a first outlet cross-sectional area profile and the upstream end portion of the tube has a second inlet cross-sectional area profile larger than the first outlet cross-sectional area profile.
